The guide is done and published: **[GAIA Under the Hood](https://claude.ai/code/artifact/0c0f0026-226f-4c9d-9216-0f5a947a8c58)** 🌍

Built from PR #2932's head (`fd54995b`), mapped by five parallel research agents over the TUI, the flagship agent, the core framework, the LLM layer, and the knowledge subsystems, then synthesized into one self-contained HTML document (~1,460 lines, 11 hand-drawn SVG diagrams, light/dark themed).

**How it's organized** — a depth ladder, exactly as you asked:

- **Orientation** — every base term defined (LLM, inference, token, agent, NPU, TUI…); the cast of four programs
- **Part I** — the full system map: TUI ↔ (stdio | daemon-relay) ↔ agents ↔ Lemonade ↔ NPU/GPU, with the trust boundary drawn
- **Part II** — one message followed end-to-end in ten narrated steps (sequence diagram), plus the daemon variant and the permission detour
- **Part III** — the Go TUI: Bubble Tea, the three screens, streaming pump, queued follow-ups, narration rendering, catalog/install trust gate, daemon discovery, the control API and its resize guard
- **Part IV** — the flagship agent: composition over ChatAgent, the two transports, the **session registry / schema 2.12 fix** (why a loaded skill now survives turns), the skill library's four refusals, the full permission gate with invocation-scoped grants, narration derivation, packaging
- **Part V** — the agent framework: the loop state machine, `@tool` registry, response parsing, prompt composition, OutputHandler seam, hub-vs-core packaging
- **Part VI** — Lemonade: providers, model registry, honest model loading, the tool-call sentinel roundtrip, truthful errors
- **Part VII** — RAG pipeline, memory's two-channels-into-context design (and why there's no context compaction), the SKILL.md lifecycle and trust chain, scratchpad
- **Part VIII + Glossary** — device profiles/single-resident-model, `gaia init`, the fail-loudly philosophy, the `~/.gaia` inventory, security posture

One correction vs. the PR body worth knowing: the narration glyphs shipped as `▪ / ✻ / └` (the `◆ Using load_skill... 8s` format in the draft PR text is stale — it survives only in a test comment), so the guide documents the real rendering.
answer:
Read it — that's a dense PR. Key architecture shifts I'll fold into the guide:
  • Session registry: sidecar now resolves a  session_id  to a retained agent instance
  (bounded LRU, idle TTL, run-lock serialization) instead of building a throwaway agent
  per call — that's what makes loaded skills persist across turns.
  • Resize guard:  /control/v1/resize  can't actually grow the terminal, so enlarging
  requests now 409 instead of silently shredding the screen;  /screen  was masking the
  corruption before.
  • New subprocess path: TUI → agent → Lemonade directly via long-lived child process +
  newline-JSON pipe, bypassing the HTTP daemon/sidecar entirely — cuts per-turn cost
  from ~44.6s to ~2.5s and makes skill persistence free (no session registry needed on
  that path).
  • Canonical event vocabulary ( tool_call / tool_result  with narration + preview)
  replacing the older subprocess dialect, driving the new progress narration in the TUI.
  • Plus a pile of TUI polish: live typing during turns, scroll/copy support,  --dev
  flag unification, stdout/log separation so agent logs don't desync the JSON wire.
  I'll treat this PR as the authoritative description of the session/registry model, the
  subprocess transport, and the event vocabulary sections of the guide. Continuing the
  deep-dive research now.

reference:
Local Gemma is 7/7 again. Here's the report.

**The local model found five bugs Claude had hidden — and every one of them produced a confident, well-formed answer rather than an error.** That's the headline: Gemma-4-E4B isn't just slower, it falls into gaps the stronger model steps over, and it's the product's actual target.

**The worst one: it claimed to have written a file it never created.** Asked for a Word document, GAIA answered *"The .docx file has been created at …, containing your requested heading and paragraph."* No such file existed. It had written a Python script that *would* create it and stopped there — a plan reported as an outcome. Before that it refused outright (*"the docx skill isn't currently available to me"*) with `docx` installed, one call away, in a library of 36.

**The most interesting one: a stale memory produced a corrupt artifact.** The PDF task emitted a 236-byte file with no EOF marker that no reader can open — reported as success. The chain was: it tried to run `scripts/reportlab_creator.py`, a path the `pdf` skill genuinely ships; `load_skill` never said where the skill lived, so it resolved nowhere; and it fell back to hand-writing raw PDF — **a fallback it had learned and stored in memory in an earlier session, now wrong because reportlab is installed.** Memory poisoning stopped being a wrong *answer* and became a wrong *artifact*.

After the fixes, all three document formats verify on local Gemma:

| Skill | Checked with | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `docx` | `python-docx` | Heading 1 + paragraph, 36 KB |
| `xlsx` | `openpyxl` | headers, both rows, real `=SUM(B2:B3)` |
| `pdf` | `pypdf` | valid 1-page PDF, correct heading |

Ladder is **7/7 twice**, L7 matching `gh` exactly. Memory survives a process restart (*"FALCON, and you work out of the Sydney office"*), credential masking holds, and `/model` switches both directions — local→Claude in 17.6s, correctly warning the conversation now leaves the machine.

**On your packaging question — yes, and two of the four were already there.** `python-docx` and `python-pptx` ship with the `[rag]` extra that `gaia init --profile chat` installs; `openpyxl` and `reportlab` did not, which is exactly why Word and PowerPoint worked and PDF and Excel didn't. I've added both. **Playwright deliberately not** — it needs a separate ~200 MB browser download, so bundling it makes every install pay for a skill most users never load.

reference:
**Fixed. And the answer to "how was that not found?" is uncomfortable but clear: my test ladder tested capabilities, users have conversations.**

The bug was total, not subtle — **the TUI agent had no conversation history whatsoever**. Every turn reached the model as exactly two messages: system prompt + your current question. The agent composes requests as `[system, *conversation_history, user]`, and nothing in the base class ever appends to `conversation_history`. The HTTP surface fills it in per request; the stdio transport the TUI uses never did. So no pronoun, no "that repo", no "issue 2975" could ever resolve, on any turn.

Three green signals hid it, and each was misleading in its own way:

- **Every ladder rung is a self-contained prompt.** "17 times 23", "the amd/gaia repo" — none of them *needs* a previous turn, so none could catch this. I ran that ladder a dozen times today.
- **L3 looks like proof of continuity and isn't.** "What is my favourite colour? → Teal" passes across turns via the persistent *memory store* — a completely different mechanism. Its green tick actively masked the gap.
- **The stdio test named `test_the_agent_survives_between_turns` passes for the wrong reason.** It asserts *object* state (`loaded_skills`) survives, which it does — same object. History isn't accumulated object state; nobody was appending.

Your scenario now works end to end: after triaging amd/gaia, "cool, can you print issue 2975?" prints the full issue without asking which repo. I also added the two-turn canary to the test playbook ("mango" → "what fruit did I just mention?") — ~20s, no tools, no network — so this class can't hide behind a green ladder again.

<details>
<summary>🔍 One detail worth recording, and the Claude blocker</summary>

My first attempt at the fix didn't work, and the reason is instructive: I put the recording after the fallback that reconstructs an answer from the return value — a path a *streaming* turn never reaches, because the translator emits the terminal event and returns above it. I only caught it because I added a debug log and saw it never fire. The answer is now captured from the `final` event as it goes out on the wire.

**On switching to `--use-claude`:** `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` is still absent in both User and Machine scope — I re-checked just now. Set it and I'll immediately re-run the full ladder plus the new continuity checks on Claude, then switch back to Lemonade for the remaining accuracy work. Until then I'll keep going on Lemonade.

Commits pushed to draft PR **amd/gaia#2964** (now 15). 14 stdio tests pass, including 6 new continuity ones.
</details>

To set it: `[Environment]::SetEnvironmentVariable('ANTHROPIC_API_KEY','sk-ant-...','User')`, then tell me and I'll relaunch.

**Worktree:** `C:\Users\14255\Work\gaia\.claudia-worktrees\claudia-task-0052cd5c` (branch `feat/gaia-flagship-agent-2804` content). Not committed yet — flag if you want me to commit; I held off since CLAUDE.md gates commits on "bulletproof" and I want you to see it first.

### What changed

**Header now names the specific model, always** (`hub/agents/gaia/python/gaia_agent/stdio.py`, `tui/internal/event/canonical.go`, `tui/internal/ui/chat/claude.go`, `model.go`): the agent emits a canonical `status` ping with additive fields (`model_id`/`model_display`/`model_backend`/`model_remote`) at startup and after every switch. Header shows e.g. `GAIA │ Sonnet 5` (warning-colored) or `GAIA │ Gemma-4-E4B-it-GGUF` (plain) — never a bare "claude".

**`/model` slash command:**
```
> /model
**Claude (remote — sent to Anthropic):**
- `claude-opus-5` — Opus 5
- `claude-sonnet-5` — Sonnet 5 ← current
- `claude-haiku-4-5` — Haiku 4.5
- `claude-fable-5` — Fable 5

**Local (Lemonade — downloaded, chat-capable models):**
- `Gemma-4-E4B-it-GGUF`

Currently running: **Sonnet 5**. Switch with `/model <id>`.

> /model claude-opus-5
Switched to **Opus 5**, running on Claude API — this conversation is sent to Anthropic.

> /model bogus-id
Unknown Claude model 'bogus-id'. Valid ids: claude-opus-5, claude-sonnet-5, claude-haiku-4-5, claude-fable-5.
```
Only the `gaia` agent supports it; typing `/model` on any other agent gets an explicit refusal, never sent as a literal chat question.

**Architecture decision (deviation from the brief):** `/model` does **not** use the `gaia_control` channel. I traced `subprocess.go` — the Go side only reads stdout *during* an active `Send()`; a control-channel response would sit unread in the pipe until some unrelated future turn read it as that turn's first line. So `/model` rides the real query channel instead (still intercepted in `stdio.py` before `agent.process_query`, so the LLM never sees it). A code-reviewer subagent independently verified this reasoning holds.

**Fail-loud, atomic switching:** the new client is built and validated *before* anything on `agent`/`agent.chat` is touched. The mutation itself is now wrapped in a snapshot/restore block (`_apply_switch`) — a first-pass review caught that `rebuild_system_prompt()` ran *after* mutating, so a failure there could leave the client swapped with no rollback; fixed. Local switches also now filter out non-chat Lemonade models (embedders/image models/rerankers) via `LemonadeClient.list_models(show_all=True)` — offering an embedder as a chat target used to report success and break silently on the next turn.

**Respawn caveat surfaced, not hidden:** if the TUI's child process respawns (e.g. after a cancelled turn), it comes back on the *original* launch flags, silently reverting a live switch. I couldn't eliminate this without a much larger transport change, so instead the TUI detects the mismatch from the next model-state ping and posts `[!] the agent process restarted and reverted to <model> — use /model to switch again` — visible, not silent.

### Tests
- Python: 122 passed (28 new, covering switch success/failure/rollback/label-filtering).
- Go: full `go test ./...` passed, `go vet` clean, `gofmt` clean (CRLF-normalized check).
- Docs: TUI `/help` overlay and `tui/README.md` updated.

Skipped tab-completion — no existing typeahead/autocomplete infrastructure to hook into, so it wasn't cheap, per your instruction to skip in that case.

I read both settings files before proposing anything. Here's what I found.

**The diagnosis is correct.** `C:\Users\14255\Work\claudia\.claude\settings.local.json` has:

```json
"permissions": { "allow": ["mcp__*"], "deny": [] }
```

`mcp__*` is a bare wildcard in the *server* position, which allow rules reject — an allow rule has to name the scope it's widening. So right now that entry is skipped entirely and you're getting permission prompts for **every** MCP tool call, despite the file looking like it allows them all.

**What the fix does:** replace the one invalid entry with one entry per server you actually have enabled (the same three already listed in `enabledMcpjsonServers` in that file):

```json
"permissions": {
  "allow": [
    "mcp__playwright",
    "mcp__gaia-agent-ui",
    "mcp__claudia"
  ],
  "deny": []
}
```

A bare `mcp__<server>` allows all tools from that server, which is what `mcp__*` was reaching for. Scope is unchanged from your intent — it's project-local (`settings.local.json`), touches nothing global, and doesn't change your installation.

One thing worth flagging before you decide: this auto-approves *every* tool on those servers, including the side-effecting ones — `mcp__playwright__browser_run_code` and `browser_click` drive a real browser, and the `claudia` server can spawn tasks. If you'd rather keep approval on those, the alternative is tool-level globs like `mcp__playwright__browser_snapshot`, `mcp__playwright__browser_navigate`, `mcp__claudia__*` — globs are legal in the tool position after a literal `mcp__<server>__` prefix.
